item.title: NASA's Van Allen Probe A burns up over the Pacific after 14 years in space

item.title: How do black holes generate magnetic fields?

item.title: An ancient shockwave | Astronomy Magazine
item.description: Gavin Bent/Kaleb Jordan SNR G206.9+2.3 is all that remains of a star that exploded in Monoceros about 7,000 light-years away. Arguably overshadowed by neighboring objects like the Rosette Nebula, this object features delicate, nested shells of emission caused by the supernova’s blast wave as it plows through surrounding gas and dust.
